finalText:
I went through all 380 commits and the PR sheet. Most of it really was dependency bumps, refactor-only renames, and test/CI churn — I excluded all of that. What's left in `CHANGELOG.md` under **4.2.0** is everything that actually touches behavior a consumer of this package would notice:

- **Breaking**: expired tokens now return 401 instead of 403 — the one real compatibility risk in this release.
- **Added**: automatic exponential-backoff retry for failed webhook deliveries (the only `feat` commit in the whole range).
- **Fixed**: 10 bullets, each one collapsing a fix that landed repeatedly across modules (e.g. "guard the null cursor" hit queue/api/webhooks/db separately — that's one line, not four) — pagination null-cursor crashes, empty allow-list handling, duplicate headers, double-trimmed trailing slashes, trace ID loss on retry, mislabeled histogram units, unclear token-parser errors, an HTTP timer leak, an unclosed shutdown pool, and full request bodies leaking into logs.

I left out the perf commits (batched metric writes, skipped JSON round-trips, schema reuse, etc.) — they're real but there's no benchmark data in the history to back a concrete claim, so I didn't want to put unverifiable numbers in front of users. Let me know if you want a line added anyway, or if any of the fix groupings should be split back out/attributed differently.
